requirements.title: Continuation skips comment lines and omits continuation markers
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p1, first four sentences, and p2 next-line selection; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 8-10 and 14-15.
requirements.definition: A continuation marker connects a statement to the next noncomment line rather than necessarily the immediately adjacent physical line. Interposed comment lines remain commentary. An ampersand occurring in a comment does not continue that comment or otherwise affect source interpretation. An ampersand serving as a continuation marker contributes no character to the statement. The pinned subclause specifies no numeric continuation-line ceiling; its separate statement-size and physical-line restrictions still apply.
requirements.oracle: An ordinary program checks independently known integer results across comment-interrupted continuations and verifies that a comment ending in an ampersand does not swallow the next assignment. A raw character assignment contains exactly 256 continuation lines, each carrying a nonempty part of one token, and checks all 256 x characters followed by Z. It has 261 logical statement characters and short physical lines; continuation markers are not character data.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The long-chain case is a bounded F2023 witness, not a proof of unlimited processor resources. It intentionally crosses the earlier 255-continuation-line rule, which is not present in the pinned F2023 text. A reference selected in f2018 mode cannot establish rejection of this F2023-valid input as a fixture defect. Character resumption and token splitting are necessary but uncredited dependencies of that witness; their distinct restrictions and text effects have separate requirements below.
requirements.dependencies: 6.3.2.3 defines every skipped comment-line form. 6.3.2.4 p3-p4 define the continued token and character contexts. 6.3.2.1 and 6.3.2.6 impose 10000-character physical lines and one-million-character statements. 4.2 p2(1), PDF 46, retains processor size/complexity qualifications.

requirements.title: An ampersand alone cannot supply the nonblank source of a line
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p1, final sentence; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 10-12.
requirements.definition: A physical line cannot have an ampersand as its sole nonblank character. Nor can the only nonblank source before a comment-introducing exclamation point be an ampersand. An ampersand within an actual comment or character datum is not that forbidden source-line shape.
requirements.oracle: Two raw diagnose manifests isolate the forbidden shapes between complete statements. Each repair inserts one initial exclamation point, changing that line into commentary while leaving all other bytes unchanged. The repairs run an initialized scalar check. A negative requires a diagnostic at the offending physical line, not arbitrary rejection or a successful compile-only control.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The source requires reporting capability under 4.2 p2(5), not a fatal exit. Located errors are accepted independently of ordinary exit status. The bare-ampersand fixture additionally qualifies the exact observed GNU f951 warning and its parsed line through a sole, hash-verified free-form compilation input with no INCLUDE or competing source attribution. That inference is explicit in the manifest and result, not a fabricated filename in compiler output. Wrong-file/line, unrelated-message, wrong-step, crash and timeout exclusions remain. No generic warning, portability, or missing-space allowance is imported from other cases.
requirements.dependencies: 6.3.2.3 distinguishes commentary from source and character data. 4.2 p2(5), PDF 46, supplies Clause 6 diagnostic capability.

requirements.title: Noncharacter continuation requires a terminal marker and a successor line
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p2; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 13-16.
requirements.definition: For continuation outside character context, the first line's last nonblank source character must be an ampersand, possibly followed by commentary. A subsequent noncomment line must exist. On that next noncomment line, a first-nonblank ampersand is optional for inter-token continuation: if present, resumption is immediately after it; if absent, resumption includes the line from its first character position. The split-token rule in p3 is a stricter condition, not an exception that can be ignored.
requirements.oracle: One positive-control program exercises terminal markers, markers before comments, and both optional leading-marker forms with defined arithmetic results. Two diagnose pairs remove a required trailing marker or transpose it with the preceding plus sign; their otherwise identical repairs run the value 3. The transposed-marker manifest qualifies the observed Flang warning about a missing comment introducer. A third pair puts a terminal ampersand on an otherwise complete END PROGRAM and follows it only with a comment. Removing exactly that ampersand gives the compile-only repair. The negative's declared span runs from the END line through the observed one-past-final-record EOF position, with continuation/EOF/ampersand-specific message predicates. No other program tokens, literal delimiters or END statements are missing.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Outside character context, ignoring a few extra inter-token blanks cannot distinguish all implementation start-column choices; the resumption definition is preserved without inventing an independent observable effect. The malformed expressions are not merely alternate legal statements. The missing-successor pair accepts a qualified report at the terminal marker or its EOF event, not a fictitious physical record, a whole-program recovery range, or an unlocated driver summary. It neither mandates fatal rejection nor credits compiler crashes. No nonfatal predicate is allowed without specific evidence of the relevant message and attribution.
requirements.dependencies: 3.21 defines character context. 6.3.2.2 governs noncharacter blanks; p3 governs split lexical tokens. 6.3.2.5 explains why a missing continuation does not implicitly join physical lines. 4.2 p2(5), PDF 46, requires source-form reporting, not compulsory rejection.

requirements.title: A split lexical token resumes immediately after a leading ampersand
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p3; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 17-18.
requirements.definition: When one lexical token spans physical lines, the first noncomment successor must have an ampersand as its first nonblank character. The remaining characters of that token start directly after that marker, with no intervening blank. This mandatory leading marker differs from the optional marker between tokens in p2.
requirements.oracle: A positive-control program splits a name, INTEGER keyword, integer literal, and power operator, with a comment between the name fragments, and checks small defined results. Two raw name-assignment pairs respectively omit the required leading marker and insert a blank after it. Their repairs insert that one marker or delete that one blank. Each negative declares the two-line assignment span, accepting a primary report on either part or a range contained within those lines. Both pieces are necessary to form the declared name, so the negative is not a different valid assignment.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Four token classes are finite representatives, not new ownership of R603, R708, R1008, labels, or all token spellings. The source also applies to character tokens, whose more specific context is handled separately by p4. Accepted repairs are positive controls rather than full effect coverage of a reporting restriction. GNU's first-line reports and the successor-line reports concern the same isolated assignment. An unrelated location, competing file, driver summary or whole-program recovery span does not satisfy the explicitly bounded oracle.
requirements.dependencies: 6.2.1 defines lexical tokens (PDF 68), 6.2.2/R603 names, 5.5.2 statement keywords, R708 integer literals, and R1008 the power operator. 6.3.2.2 forbids interior token blanks outside its exceptions. 4.2 p2(5), PDF 46, supplies source-form reporting.

requirements.title: Character-context continuation requires markers on both sides
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p4, marker and successor conditions; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 19-21.
requirements.definition: Inside either character context, the final nonblank character of a continued line must be an ampersand. A later noncomment line is required, and that next noncomment line must start, apart from blanks, with an ampersand. An exclamation point still inside the character context is data, not permission to put a comment after an otherwise nonterminal marker.

pending.missing-later-line-diagnostic: Source-only pending isolation and reporting oracle: truncating a character continuation at EOF also leaves its literal and enclosing program unit incomplete. A missing-END error is not evidence for this specific condition. Next step: independently establish an isolated continuation-specific EOF witness and narrowly qualified EOF reporting support; retain this facet pending rather than accepting generic parse failure or adding fatal-rejection policy.

requirements.oracle: A positive-control program continues apostrophe and quote literals and a character string edit descriptor across valid paired markers, including an intervening comment. Two byte-preserved pairs omit the leading or terminal marker from a short character assignment. Repaired controls change only that one marker and check the exact value. Diagnose expects the physical line with the missing marker. The missing-leading-marker case permits only the observed GNU warning about a missing ampersand in a continued character constant and the observed Flang portability message about the absent preceding ampersand; each predicate is family-, severity-, message-, file-, and line-qualified. These are reporting oracles, not invented fatal-rejection requirements.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A compiler may diagnose an unterminated literal on the preceding line instead of the missing leading marker on its successor; the report must preserve that location difference, not silently broaden the oracle. These positive controls establish admission, not detection of the separate missing-successor condition. A comment-like exclamation point in character data must not be treated as actual trailing commentary.
requirements.dependencies: 3.21 includes literals and character string edit descriptors. 7.4.4.3/R724 and 13.2.1/13.9 retain literal/FORMAT semantics. 6.3.2.3 supplies comment-line classification. 4.2 p2(5), PDF 46, supplies reporting capability.

requirements.title: Character continuation preserves data blanks but excludes layout and markers
requirements.source: 6.3.2.4 p4, resumption rule under its marker conditions; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, lines 19-21.
requirements.definition: With valid character-continuation markers, character text resumes directly after the successor's leading ampersand. Blanks before the trailing marker within the character context and blanks after the leading marker belong to the character text. Layout blanks after the trailing marker or before the leading marker do not. An ampersand that is ordinary character data is distinct from an adjacent ampersand serving as a continuation marker.
requirements.oracle: A raw fixture preserves two data blanks before and after continuation markers, three layout blanks after a trailing marker, and four layout blanks before a leading marker. Both literal delimiter styles must yield the exact eight-character value with four internal blanks. Positional substring assertions check the suffix positions and the four-blank regions without using another multi-blank literal as the sole oracle. A continued FORMAT descriptor produces the specified seven-character internal record after an IOSTAT guard. A separate literal places a data ampersand immediately before a continuation marker. In addition to a full value comparison, IACHAR results 38, 33, and 59 independently check its three punctuation positions.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The fixture deliberately uses external metadata so header injection or whitespace normalization cannot alter the evidence. All character objects are initialized before assignment or internal output, and no undefined or out-of-bounds data are inspected. It does not test doubled-quote spelling or the entire processor character repertoire.
requirements.dependencies: 3.21 defines the two contexts; 6.3.2.2 preserves internal character blanks. 7.4.4.3 distinguishes literal delimiters from values; 13.9 supplies the character edit descriptor output effect. 9.4.1 and 16.9.98 (PDF 151/416) justify fixed in-bounds substrings and IACHAR on known ASCII characters, without assuming native ASCII encoding. 6.3.2.4 p1 excludes marker characters from the statement.

accounting.rationale: PDF 72, lines 8-12: selection, comment behavior, marker elision, and both forbidden ampersand-only shapes are distinct.
All 6.3.2.3 comment-line forms may intervene without being continuation lines containing statement text.
PDF 72, lines 13-16: distinguish both terminal-marker positions, existence and selection of a successor, and both resumption alternatives.
The missing-successor diagnostic facet remains explicitly pending; conforming controls do not close it.
When present as first nonblank, the marker defines the resume position immediately after itself; p3 can make it mandatory.
Without a leading marker, resumption starts at physical character position one, including any inter-token blanks, not at an invented first-nonblank position.
PDF 72, lines 17-18: preserve token splitting as the premise and the three conditions on its successor.
PDF 72, lines 19-21: marker/existence/selection restrictions and the resulting character text are separately testable.
An EOF truncation must not receive credit solely from an unavoidable missing-END or unrelated literal diagnostic.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and verified integration repairs: doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_005.json. Inter-token, split-token and character continuations retain their separate premises, marker rules, significant blanks and comment behavior. Reporting spans and the qualified GNU warning implement RP1/RP2. The new complete-END EOF pair closes only the noncharacter missing-successor facet; the character-context counterpart remains pending.
